newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end 1.5 pct up in broad rebound.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end 1.5 pct up in broad rebound.

text.p: The Australian share market ended on a firm note on Friday as stocks rebounded from losses earlier in the week, supported by a stronger bond market, postive earnings reports and some talk about another official rate cut.
The All Ordinaries index rose 38.8 points to 2,666.2, but still 1.7 percent down on the week. Turnover was a modest A$651 million.
"The market had taken quite a beating this week, and people were generally calling it up today. Every sector rose quite solidly," one senior institutional delaer in Sydney said.
"The market expects another quarter to half a point cut in (official interest) rates," said David Perry of Austock Brokers.

The banking sector got a last minute push on news that the government had cut the pensioner deeming rate by one percentage point, but several banks immediately expressed disappointment and said they had wanted a cut of at least 1.5 points.

NAB jumped 30.2 cents to A$19.21, and Colonial 10 cents to A$3.65 following Thursday's earnings report. ANZ finished 23 cents up at A$10.25 after it said it plans to make major investments in 1998/99 as part of its strategy to expand global operations.

Thursday's strong annual results from financial services and construction conglomerate Lend Lease and construction and contract mining group Leighton Holdings inspired investors, gearing up for coming reports in the next few weeks.
Lend Lease showed a 15 percent net profit increase and a lift in final dividend to 50 cents a share, and although the stock came off early highs, it ended 35.3 cents up at A$29.32,
Leighton rose another 23 cents to A$6.35 as players took in a record profit and a special dividend.
The big miners were strong perfomers, recouping some of the losses earlier this month.
Bellwether BHP climbed 28 cents to A$17.50 and WMC firmed 16.1 cents to A$7.471.

The gold sector leaped almost 2.3 percent despite weaker bullion, and dealers said there was continued U.S. buying behind the gains. Normandy Mining firmed four cents to A$1.61 ahead of next week's result announcement.
Gold miner Sons of Gwalia reported a net loss of A$128.39 million in the year to June 30 after a write-dwon of mining and explorations property, but the stock still closed 15 cents higher at A$4.90.
Brambles rose 90 cents to A$27.70 and helped the transport sector index rise 2.6 percent.

Another winner was Mayne Nickless, up 22 cents to A$8.26 on increasing hopes of a quick sale of its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications after a government decision to ease foreign shareholder restrictions in Optus.
News Corp climbed sevem cents to A$5.95 ahead of its results on Wednesday, while Fairfax rose three to A$3.19 pending the earnings report on Tuesday.
Great Central Mines rose five cents to A$2.57 after dismissing rumours of a takeover bid from Canada's Barrick Gold.

QNI was one of the more noticeable losers, down seven cents to A$2.18 on investor worries related to the propsed merger with Billiton, a unit of South Africa's Gencor. Colombian authorities have launched a formal inquiry into the sale of the Cerro Matoso nickel mine to Billiton.
